text.p: Bonds ended close to historic highs as the market bet on the Bank of Portugal cutting interest rates on Friday at the start of a new commercial bank reserve period.
"Despite some profit-taking, the support along the curve is very strong," said one trader.

Traders pointed to the rate cut in Spain, statements by a Bundesbank Council official about how the Bank could not be indifferent to Germany's economic weakness and the strength of the escudo as factors pointing to a cut by the Bank of Portugal.
The short to medium end of the curve was again the most active and the most supported, traders said. The longer end will continue to march in step with Spain, they added.

Seven out of nine economists polled in Lisbon by Reuters said they believed the Bank would cut its drain rate on Friday, with most expecting it to come down 20 basis points from its current 6.20 percent.
Only three forecast a reduction in the repo which was cut 20 basis points to 6.5 percent last week.
